To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

antioxidant expression is preserved in aorta from wild type and MnSOD deficient mice, but is reduced in aortic valves, and that MnSOD deficiency results in aortic endothelial dysfunction that is not improved with NAD(P) H oxidase inhibition.
antioxidant and sirtuins gene expression is preserved with age in aorta, whereas expression of these genes is reduced in aortic valves.
aortic valve function is not altered with aging and Mn SOD haploinsuficiency in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of aging on the cardiovascular system.
the mechanisms that regulate the aging process and age-related disease.
the role of oxidative stress in the pathogenesis of vascular dysfunction with aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study suggest that MnSOD deficiency is not associated with cardiovascular dysfunction in mice, but that antioxidant gene transcriptional responses to aging are different in aorta and the aortic valve and that MnSOD haplosufficiency is associated with aortic valve endothelial dysfunction.

MnSOD deficiency does not accelerate age-related endothelial dysfunction, but that the transcriptional response is tissue specific and that MnSOD haplodeficiency may impair the ability of NAD(P)(H) oxidase inhibition to improve endothelial function with aging.

the results of the study suggest that the aortic valve may be more sensitive to oxidative stress than the aorta and that MnSOD deficiency does not alter the age-related transcriptional response to oxidative stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aorta is relatively well protected from aging-related oxidative damage, and MnSOD appears to have a limited role in protecting against age-related endothelial dysfunction.
MnSOD is not essential for maintaining endothelial and aortal valve function with aging.
MnSOD haplodeficiency does not alter the aging process in the aorta and aorta valve, and that antioxidant gene transcription in these tissues appears to be well maintained.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are tissue-specific differences in antioxidant and siren gene expression with aging, and these differences may be important in determining the differential susceptibility to age-related cardiovascular diseases.
the aorta and aorta valve are two distinct vascular beds that respond to aging and MnSod haploinsufficency in different ways.
MnSOD deficiency results in age-associated increases in oxidative stress, which is associated with increased expression of the senescence marker p16(ink 4a), but not endothelial dysfunction.
